title: Engineer II
jobDescription: CORRELATION ONE Correlation One is the largest provider of AI and data workforce development programs globally, having trained over 500,000 professionals across 11 countries. As the largest training provider for Amazon Career Choice, and a growing partner to state governments building registered apprenticeship programs, Correlation One sits at the intersection of employer talent needs and scalable workforce training. We work with Fortune 500 enterprises, federal and state government agencies, and leading employers to close skills gaps in AI, data analytics, cybersecurity, and operations leadership. Our programs produce job-ready graduates who are prepared to contribute from day one. Your impact Software Engineers are at the center of the engineering teams at Correlation One . As an Engineer II, you build features and services within your team's technical blueprint and ship high-quality, well-tested code to production. You take on tasks that carry some ambiguity and grow your ownership over time, learning the culture of craftsmanship within your team along the way. You are open to mentorship on technology, craft, and leadership, and you help sustain an inclusive culture where everyone is heard, respected, and empowered. A day in the life Build and ship features and services within your team's architecture Help migrate rapidly-prototyped applications into production-grade, well-architected cloud services Take on development tasks that carry some ambiguity, asking good questions to close the gaps Participate in code reviews and uphold the team's standards for engineering and operational excellence Write, review, and update technical documentation Collaborate across the team to deliver quality work at a steady pace Your expertise 2-3 years of professional software development experience (ready to own meaningful work with minimal guidance) Proficiency in at least one modern language such as Python or Java Comfortable working with relational databases (we use Postgres) Familiarity with version control, code review, and automated testing as part of normal delivery Strong communication skills, especially in a remote, async-friendly team Preferred qualifications Exposure to building cloud-based services or microservices Working knowledge of relational and non-relational databases and unstructured storage Experience with React on the front end Familiarity with our stack: Python, Java, FastAPI, Spring Boot, React, Postgres, Kubernetes, GCP, GHA A Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience Where you are This role is remote and based in Latin America, with working hours that overlap the US Eastern time zone (EST). We are headquartered in New York City and have office space in Midtown Manhattan. title: Lead Instructor: Aerospace Technician
jobDescription: Correlation One is the largest provider of AI and data workforce development programs globally, having trained over 500,000 professionals across 11 countries. Our programs produce job-ready graduates who are prepared to contribute from day one. Job Summary: Lead Instructors at Correlation One are responsible for delivering high-quality, live, virtual instruction and partnering with company personnel to drive exceptional learning outcomes. Their main focus as educators is to conduct large synchronous online lectures on technical content, training anywhere from 100 to 8,000+ diverse Fellows at a time, depending on the program. This role involves preparing and leading virtual classroom sessions, collaborating with operations personnel, and contributing to the overall success of the program. Program Specific Information: The exact dates and times for this program and currently TBD, with an anticipated launch for mid July of 2026. We are proactively identifying instructors for this program and will provident updates when exact dates/times are confirmed. Virtual Classroom Leadership: Prepare and lead virtual classroom sessions for a range of Fellows, which may vary in size from 200 to 8,000+. Deliver instruction on skills tailored to Learners' needs, including math, verbal reasoning, and technical problem-solving. Oversee the management of class time Q&A and monitor chat flow, and overall class energy and engagement dynamics Collaboration: Collaborate closely with Correlation One operations personnel to ensure smooth program delivery and adherence to schedules. Be flexible in contributing to classes during weekdays and/or weekends, as program schedules vary. Assist in lesson design, development, and improvement which may include tracking edits, suggestions, or changes to curriculum as needed Expectations: In addition to the core responsibilities, Lead Instructors are expected to adhere to the following expectations: Professionalism: Interact professionally with Fellows, Correlation One staff, additional contractors, and guest speakers, maintaining a high level of courtesy and respect. Lecture Preparation: Diligently and adequately prepare for lectures to ensure the delivery of high-quality content. Dynamic Online Presence Responsiveness and Empathy: Be highly responsive and empathetic to Fellows, providing thoughtful answers and assistance throughout the lesson Adjust the lesson pace and presentation to meet the needs of diverse Fellows while also maintaining responsibility for timely delivery of the prepared content. Exhibit an energy, pacing, and ability to make complex topics accessible and maintain strong learner engagement Communication: Communicate respectfully, recognizing that online or written communication may lack tone. Maintain extra communicative contact with Correlation One personnel. Positive Attitude: Foster a healthy learning environment by maintaining a positive attitude and promoting a culture of learning. Course Improvement: Contribute to course improvement by providing thoughtful and transparent feedback to the Correlation One team. Your expertise 5+ years of hands-on experience in aerospace, advanced manufacturing, or related technical environments (Structures, Assembly & Integration, or Composites preferred) Familiarity with technician-level skills aligned to aerospace roles, including blueprint reading, precision measurement tools, and hands-on work in structures, assembly & integration, or composites (e.g., drilling/fastening, system assembly, torque application, or composite layup/bonding) Comfort with digital collaboration tools (e.g., Zoom, Slack, Microsoft Office) Experience with safety and quality standards (e.g., OSHA, 5S, FOD) Experience working from written work instructions, engineering drawings, and quality specifications in a production or aerospace environment Demonstrated depth in at least one of the following: Structures (drilling, fastening, structural assembly), Assembly & Integration (system assembly, fluid systems, harness routing), or Composites (layup, bonding, surface prep) Experience teaching, training, or mentoring adult learners in technical subjects Ability to deliver engaging instruction in a live, virtual environment at scale Strong communication and presentation skills Where you are This role is remote and can be located anywhere.
